digest.component_or_area: DC harness field-readiness gate and epic-link probe
propositions: The DC harness errors all 62 cells at fixture setup because wait_for_jira_dc_ready gates on Epic Link/Epic Name fields that do not exist until the first Jira Software project is created, forming an ordering deadlock where the gate blocks the action that would provision those fields.

Experiment 30981084637 proves the deadlock: after 180s of silent waiting, Epic Link/Epic Name remain absent (27 fields, zero customfield_* entries), but appear immediately (0.0512s) after creating the pinned GreenHopper scrum project, eliminating budget and degrade hypotheses.

The decision rule in not_ready_message ('no customfield_* entries means plugin still starting') is wrong for a normal Jira Software instance with no project, causing misdiagnosis of the root cause as a timing shortfall rather than an ordering violation.

The Epic-field capability check must move from session-start (wait_for_jira_dc_ready) to post-provisioning (_assert_project_capabilities), the only call site where those fields can exist, while maintaining the bounded wait and loud failure on genuine degrade.

The deterministic probe (jira_dc_epic_link_clear_probe.py) has the same ordering bug: _await_named_fields runs before project creation, causing probe runs 30944211742 and 30930839323 to fail identically since change 1387.
Live verification run 30982731669 proves the fix: 62 passed, 1 xfailed, 0 failed, 0 errored, with Epic field registration consistently completing in 0.032s-0.058s after project creation.
